module_title: Advanced Hohfeldian Matrix & Jurisprudence of Possession
introduction: Tailored for advanced legal exams and UPSC Law Optional, this level explores the second half of Hohfeld's complex matrix (dealing with the power to change legal relationships) and the deep jurisprudential debate between Savigny and Salmond regarding the true nature of Possession.

core_concepts.title: Hohfeld's Second Matrix (Second-Order Rights)
core_concepts.description:
The second matrix deals with the ability to alter legal relationships.
- Jural Correlatives:
  * POWER <---> LIABILITY: If A has the *Power* to change legal relations, B has the *Liability* to be subjected to that change. (e.g., A property owner has the *Power* to sell it; the buyer has the *Liability* of having their legal status changed to 'owner').
  * IMMUNITY <---> DISABILITY: If A has *Immunity* from a legal change, B has a *Disability* (inability) to make that change. (e.g., The President has *Immunity* from criminal prosecution; the Police have a *Disability* to arrest him).

core_concepts.title: Hohfeld's Jural Opposites (Second Matrix)
core_concepts.description:
Jural Opposites:
* POWER <---> DISABILITY (If you have the power to do something, you do not have a disability).
* LIABILITY <---> IMMUNITY (If you are liable to be changed legally, you are not immune).

core_concepts.title: Savigny's Theory of Possession
core_concepts.description:
Savigny based his theory on Roman Law.
- Rule: For possession to exist, both Corpus (physical control) and Animus (intent to hold as owner / *Animus Domini*) must be absolutely present.
- The Flaw: Under Savigny's strict theory, a tenant or a bailee (who borrows an item) does NOT have legal possession because they lack the *Animus Domini* (they know they aren't the owner). This contradicts modern law which fully protects a tenant's possession.

core_concepts.title: Salmond's Theory of Possession
core_concepts.description:
Salmond modernized the concept to fit English law.
- Rule: Possession is the continuing exercise of a claim. *Corpus* is not just physical power; it is merely the realization/manifestation of the *Animus*.
- The Animus: For Salmond, the intent doesn't have to be *Animus Domini* (intent to own). It only needs to be an intent to exclude others. Therefore, a tenant DOES have legal possession because they intend to exclude everyone else (even the landlord) during the lease.

important_entities.name: Adverse Possession
important_entities.key_fact: When prolonged possession destroys original ownership.
important_entities.significance: A fascinating intersection of Fact and Law. If a trespasser occupies land (Corpus + Animus) openly, peacefully, and continuously in hostility to the true owner for a statutory period (12 years in India for private land), the true owner's title is extinguished. The trespasser's factual possession magically transforms into legal ownership.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Advanced exams test the Hohfeldian difference between Right and Power. 
- A 'Right' dictates what others MUST do (Duty). 
- A 'Power' dictates how one can CHANGE legal relations. 
Making a Will is an exercise of **Power** (changing who gets property), not a Right. The person receiving the property is under a **Liability** (their legal status changes), not a Duty.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Right-Duty, Privilege-NoRight | Power-Liability, Immunity-Disability. Memorize this sequence for the 4 pairs of Correlatives.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Mains, if asked to critique theories of possession, contrast **Savigny's strict Roman 'Animus Domini'** with **Salmond's pragmatic English 'Intent to Exclude'** to show how modern law accommodates tenants and bailees.
